title: GROUP BY Clause & Aggregation Buckets
description: Partition rows into groups, avoid non-aggregated column errors, and explore advanced ROLLUP and CUBE grouping sets.

data.text: The **`GROUP BY`** clause collapses multiple rows sharing identical values in designated columns into summary rows. Any column projected in the `SELECT` list that is not part of the `GROUP BY` clause must be enclosed within an aggregate function.

data.title: Monthly Revenue Aggregation with DATE_TRUNC
data.content: Grouping sales data by month and payment method.
data.code:
SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at) AS sales_month,
    payment_method,
    COUNT(*) AS total_transactions,
    SUM(amount) AS gross_sales
FROM transactions
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at), payment_method
ORDER BY sales_month DESC, gross_sales DESC;

data.text: Advanced: GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, and CUBE
When generating financial balance sheets and BI reports, you often need subtotals and grand totals in addition to grouped rows. `ROLLUP` produces hierarchical subtotals automatically.

data.title: Sales Report with ROLLUP Subtotals
data.content: Produces region subtotals, product subtotals, and overall grand totals.
data.code:
SELECT 
    region,
    product_category,
    SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue
FROM regional_sales
GROUP BY ROLLUP (region, product_category)
ORDER BY region NULLS LAST, product_category NULLS LAST;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Every column in `SELECT` must either appear in `GROUP BY` or be enclosed in an aggregate function.
Use `DATE_TRUNC('day' | 'month' | 'year', timestamp)` to group by time periods.
Use `ROLLUP` and `CUBE` to compute multi-level subtotals and grand totals in a single query.
